To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the nonlinear DGLAP evolution equations with recombination corrections are able to reproduce the existing parton distributions in proton and that the resulting nonlinear parton distributions can be used to describe the experimental data on the proton structure functions.

the nonlinear evolution equation is an effective tool that can be used to connect the quarks models with the data at high Q2 and that it can be used as an important ingredient for the global analysis of the parton distributions.

the nonlinear evolution equations can provide a unified approach to the description of the parton distributions in a proton and that they can improve the pertubative stability of the DGLAP evolution at low Q2.
